少有母養之恩 means she mothered him in youth, not that she raised him only briefly; the proposed “had had” is awkward.
對曰：「在吳。」 is one quoted reply; the extra quote after answered is a punctuation error.

I know life and death are decreed and longevity is heaven's gift. The Zhou and Jin kings and Yan Hui were men of supreme intellect, yet they died young—how much more I, dull and obscure, who have already outlived my share, lived as your heir, and will depart with honors few could claim? What room is left for regret?

I know life and death are decreed and longevity is heaven's gift. Prince Jin of Zhou and Yan Hui were men of supreme intellect, yet they died young—how much more I, dull and obscure, who have already outlived my share, lived as your heir, and will depart with honors few could claim? What room is left for regret?
周晉、顏回 names Prince Jin of Zhou together with Yan Hui, not kings of Zhou and of Jin.

Your servant has heard that death and life have their allotment and length and brevity come from Heaven; the kings of Zhou and Jin and Yan Hui had talents of the highest wisdom, yet still met early death—how much more your servant, stupid and mean, his years having passed his allotted span, who in life was heir of the state and in death will enjoy glorious fortune—for your servant it is already much; what grief or resentment is there!

Your servant has heard that death and life have their allotment and length and brevity come from Heaven; Prince Jin of Zhou and Yan Hui had talents of the highest wisdom, yet still met early death—how much more your servant, stupid and mean, his years having passed his allotted span, who in life was heir of the state and in death will enjoy glorious fortune—for your servant it is already much; what grief or resentment is there!
The same 周晉 is one person, Prince Jin of Zhou, not “the kings of Zhou and Jin.”
